फिल्म Ramayana की रिलीज़ में सिर्फ तीन दिन बाकी हैं और बॉक्स ऑफिस पर अभी से गदर मच गया है! 🔥

रिलीज़ से पहले ही फिल्म की वर्ल्डवाइड एडवांस बुकिंग ₹75 crore पार कर चुकी है, जिसमें भारत से 37 crore रुपये का शानदार कलेक्शन शामिल है। 💸

एग्ज़िबिटर्स और मेकर्स के बीच रेवेन्यू शेयरिंग का विवाद सुलझते ही थिएटर्स की संख्या बढ़कर 3,500 हो गई है और भारत में अब तक 9 lakh टिकटें बिक चुकी हैं। 🎟️

Ranbir Kapoor और Yash की यह फिल्म टिकटों की रफ्तार के मामले में Animal और KGF Chapter 2 को भी पीछे छोड़ चुकी है। 🚀

5 November 2026 को दुनिया भर में रिलीज़ हो रही इस फिल्म का क्रेज काफी तगड़ा बना हुआ है।

क्या आपको लगता है कि Ramayana पहले ही दिन कमाई के सारे पुराने रिकॉर्ड तोड़ देगी? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय बताइए! 🎬👇

ctx.title: Ramayana advance booking blazes past  ₹75 crore as release day approaches; Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film now outpacing Animal, KGF 2
ctx.summary: Advance bookings for Ramayana Part One are now outpacing Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's biggest hits - Animal and KGF Chapter 2, respectively.
ctx.text:
As the release day approaches for Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana , the advance bookings have finally opened in full flow. For about 10 days, a deadlock between the makers and exhibitors over revenue sharing had curtailed the advance bookings. But over the weekend, that was resolved, opening up more screens, including the crucial single screens. This has seen the film register huge jumps in advance bookings in India, while the overseas numbers continue to impress.
Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 full days before its global release. But for the next 10 days, only the Hindi version had extensive shows. And there, too, most of the single-screen and smaller centres were yet to open. But on Friday, the stalemate between the exhibitors and distributors ended as terms were reached. Since then, more theatres are opening pre-sales for the film across India each hour.
By Monday morning, the number of screens for the film had increased to 3,500, with 1,000 added in the last two days. By the morning of November 2, three days before its release, the film had grossed ₹ 37 crore in pre-sales in India. This included an impressive ₹ 22 crore from the opening day itself. The remainder is spread over its extended weekend. The Hindi version continues to lead the way, but the Kannada and Telugu versions are rapidly gaining ground now. As of Monday morning, the Kannada version had sold tickets worth almost ₹ 4 crore, while the Telugu version had also crossed ₹ 2 crore.
A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)
Ramayana has now sold almost 9 lakh tickets in pre-sales across India. The premium formats - including IMAX - are driving the sales, accounting for almost one-fourth of the sales, despite holding just 4% of the screens. This pace is faster than the lead actors' previous big hits. Ramayana is now outpacing both Ranbir Kapoor 's Animal and Yash 's KGF Chapter 2. However, it remains behind Dhurandhar 2, RRR, and Pushpa 2 so far.
What has helped Ramayana’s case is the pre-sales buzz overseas. In North America, the film will have paid previews on November 4, the eve of its release. The 24 hours after its world premiere saw the film register a 27% jump in collections. By Monday morning, the film had earned $3.9 million in overseas advance bookings, including over $1.5 million for the US paid previews alone. This takes the film’s worldwide advance-booking gross to ₹ 75 crore three days before its release.
Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part film. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will release in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.
Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the film in the Hindi-speaking market. The film is also planned for a worldwide IMAX release.
